cause: Issuer-side serving failure, not a genuine default by the holder's own work. ISSUER-A never delivered — its own capacity_model never ran to grade the work it owed. The real bug: this window's redemption tracker (packages/gate-market-agents/src/loop/redemption-tracker.ts) routed WORKER-CODE's (the holder's) own first, failed submit_job attempt to ISSUER-A as the graded verdict, and ISSUER-A correctly reported that verdict via serveRedemption(passed=false). WORKER-CODE's later, genuinely passing submit_job attempt was never re-routed to ISSUER-A because the tracker is single-serve. The window then closed with the claim unsettled. This is the first real on-chain default this testbed has produced.
resolution: Deliberately triggered via settleWindowClose (permissionless), rather than a corrected serveRedemption(passed=true), per explicit instruction: ISSUER-A never delivered, so reporting a pass would record a delivery that did not happen. The default correctly pays the holder from the issuer's bond and restores the issuer's headroom — the real invariant this window was actually testing (an issuer who never serves loses via its own bond, at real cost) held, even though the underlying cause was a software bug in the redemption tracker's routing, not a genuine capacity failure by ISSUER-A.

transaction.triggeredBy: deployer address (permissionless call — any address may trigger settleWindowClose once a claim's window has closed)

realFixesRequiredBeforeAnyFurtherRun: Contract: serveRedemption has no window-closed check, letting a late passed=true report race settleWindowClose and escape a genuine default — needs a revert-after-close guard, fuzzed, and redeployed to Base Sepolia.

Loop/role-confusion: redemption must grade the ISSUER's own delivery (via its capacity_model), never the holder's own submitted work — the redemption tracker's routing is the real root cause of this event.
